title: Relationships 2
note: B2 vocab leaf, drafted 2026-09-05 on the home lane. Pool swept twice. Two predecessors own the obvious set between them — b1_relationships (36: classmate, acquaintance, relative, in-laws, stranger, get on with, keep in touch, trust, respect, admire, rely on, loyalty, break up, fall out, quarrel, divorce, romance) and a2_family (25: relationship, couple, wedding, marry, argue, behaviour, character, community, society) — so the first sweep returned chemistry, engaged, stepmother, sibling, upbringing, household, fall for, adopt and godparent all already taught. This unit is the layer they leave: the words for how close a bond actually is (commitment, mutual, devotion, intimacy, rapport), how one goes wrong and gets repaired (drift apart, take for granted, possessive, toxic, separation, reconcile), and family shapes and circles beyond the nuclear set (stepfather, half-brother, custody, foster, peer pressure, clique, outsider). C57 card 0 recaps Relationships 1. C49 all 36 words across three boards of 12. Build-the-family card: commitment -> committed, affection -> affectionate, devotion -> devoted, reconcile -> reconciliation, all four derived forms drilled as bank items — and the same -ion/-ate machinery b2_suffixes_1 teaches directly. A12 senses on bond (between people), toxic (relationship), foster (a child) and peer (same age), each of which has a commoner everyday reading. Bands 3 B2 / 10 C1 / 23 unbanded. E10 Use is rewrite production; every underline reconstructs its answer.

cards.title: You already know
cards.note: Relationships 1 gave you the people — classmate, acquaintance, relative, flatmate, in-laws, stranger, ex — and what happens between them: get on with, keep in touch, trust, respect, admire, rely on, break up, fall out, make up. Those words come back in this unit's sentences. What is new here is how deep a bond goes, how it goes wrong, and the families and circles people actually live in.
cards.note_cz: Relationships 1 ti dal lidi — classmate, acquaintance, relative, flatmate, in-laws, stranger, ex — a co se mezi nimi děje: get on with, keep in touch, trust, respect, admire, rely on, break up, fall out, make up. Ta slova se vracejí ve větách. Nové je tu, jak hluboké to pouto je, jak se pokazí a v jakých rodinách a partách lidé opravdu žijí.
